## Frozen commentary (Turkish)

Beşinci ayetteki غثاء yalnızca kurumuş ot değildir, selin yüzünde yüzen şeydir de. Arapça onu iki ayrı kaba birden koyar: {ar:الغثاء غثاء السيل والقدر، ما يطفح ويتفرق من النبات اليابس وزبد القدر, tr:el-ğuŝâu ğuŝâu's-seyli ve'l-kıdr mâ yatfahu ve yetefarraku mine'n-nebâti'l-yâbisi ve zebedi'l-kıdr, gloss:ğuŝâ selin de tencerenin de ğuŝâsıdır; kuru bitkiden ve tencere köpüğünden yüzeye taşıp dağılandır, source:"غ ث و,B001"}. Kelime bir atasözü değeri de taşır: {ar:يضرب به المثل فيما يضيع ويذهب غير معتد به, tr:yudrabu bihi'l-meŝelu fî mâ yadîu ve yeẕhebu ğayra mu'teddin bih, gloss:kaybolup giden ve hesaba katılmayan şey için örnek olarak anılır, source:"غ ث و,B004"}. Selin öbür yüzü sudur. Surenin kelimelerinin aileleri suyun nerede toplanıp kaldığını gösterir.

İkinci ayetteki "yarattı" fiilinin ailesinde kayalardaki oyuklar vardır: {ar:الخليقة نقر في صخرة يجتمع فيه ماء السماء, tr:el-halîka nakrun fî sahratin yectemiu fîhi mâu's-semâ, gloss:halîka kayada gök suyunun toplandığı oyuktur, source:"خ ل ق,B011"}. Bu oyuklar şöyle de anlatılır: {ar:قلاتا تمسك ماء السحاب في صفاة خلقها الله فيها تسميها العرب الخلائق, tr:kılâten tumsiku mâe's-sehâbi fî safâtin halakahallâhu fîhâ tusemmîhe'l-arabu'l-halâik, gloss:Allah'ın düz kayada yarattığı ve bulut suyunu tutan çukurlar; Araplar onlara halâik der, source:"خ ل ق,B011"}. Beşinci ayetteki أحوى'nın ailesinde selin doldurduğu kıvrımlı çukurlar vardır: {ar:الحوايا التي تكون في القيعان والرياض حفائر ملتوية يملؤها ماء السيل, tr:el-havâyâ elletî tekûnu fi'l-kîâni ve'r-riyâdi hafâiru multeviyetun yemleuhâ mâu's-seyl, gloss:havâyâ düzlüklerde ve çayırlarda selin doldurduğu kıvrımlı çukurlardır, source:"ح و ي,B008"}. "Rab" kelimesinin ailesinde bol su, toplandığı için bu adı alır: {ar:الربب وهو الماء الكثير سمي بذلك لاجتماعه, tr:er-rabeb ve huve'l-mâu'l-keŝîr sumiye bi-ẕâlike li-ictimâih, gloss:rabeb boldur ve toplandığı için bu adı almıştır, source:"ر ب ب,B013"}. Yedinci ayetteki "açık" kelimesinin ailesinde kuyu temizlenir: {ar:جهرت الركية إذا كان ماؤها قد غطى الطين فنقى ذلك حتى يظهر الماء ويصفو, tr:cehertu'r-rakiyye iẕâ kâne mâuhâ kad ğattâhu't-tînu fe-nakkâ ẕâlike hattâ yezhera'l-mâu ve yesfû, gloss:suyunu çamur örtmüş kuyuyu su görünüp duruluncaya kadar temizledim, source:"ج ه ر,B008"}. Aynı ayetteki "bilir" fiilinin ailesinde de suyu bol kuyu vardır: {ar:العيلم البئر الكثيرة الماء, tr:el-aylem el-bi'ru'l-keŝîratu'l-mâ, gloss:aylem suyu bol kuyudur, source:"ع ل م,B005"}.

Dokuzuncu ayet öğütten "fayda verirse" diye söz eder, on yedinci ayet ahireti "daha kalıcı" diye niteler. Fayda, {ar:ما يستعان به في الوصول إلى الخيرات, tr:mâ yusteânu bihî fi'l-vusûli ile'l-hayrât, gloss:iyiliklere ulaşmak için yardım alınan şey, source:"ن ف ع,B001"} diye tanımlanır. Bu tanım on yedinci ayetteki "hayırlı" kelimesinin kökünü de taşır. Kalıcılık ise şudur: {ar:البقاء ثبات الشيء على حاله الأولى وهو يضاد الفناء, tr:el-bekâu ŝebâtu'ş-şey'i alâ hâlihi'l-ûlâ ve huve yudâddu'l-fenâ, gloss:bekâ bir şeyin ilk halinde sabit durmasıdır ve yok olmanın zıddıdır, source:"ب ق ي,B001"}. Bu tanımda on sekizinci ayetteki "ilk" kelimesi de vardır.

Kur'an'da bu iki yüzü bir sahnede toplayan benzetmeyi Allah verir. Gökten su iner, vadiler {ar:فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌۢ بِقَدَرِهَا, tr:fe-sâlet evdiyetun bi-kaderihâ, gloss:vadiler kendi ölçülerince akar, source:13:17}. Burada üçüncü ayetteki "ölçtü" fiilinin kökü geçer. Sel kabarık bir köpük taşır. İnsanların süs ya da eşya için ateşte erittikleri madenin de benzer bir köpüğü vardır. Sonra ayırım gelir: {ar:فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءًۭ ۖ وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ, tr:fe-emme'z-zebedu fe-yeẕhebu cufâen ve emmâ mâ yenfau'n-nâse fe-yemkuŝu fi'l-ard, gloss:köpük atılıp gider; insanlara fayda veren ise yerde kalır, source:13:17}. Kelime farklıdır, orada غثاء değil زبد geçer. Ama sahne aynıdır. Surenin beşinci, dokuzuncu ve on yedinci ayetlere dağıttığı döküntü, fayda ve kalıcılık bu ayette tek bir selin içinde bir aradadır. Bu yan yana koyuş surenin kendi sözü değildir, ama bu ayet ona Kur'an'dan bir dayanak verir. Fayda verirse sunulan öğüt, kayadaki oyukta tutulan suya benzer. Çerçöp ise akıntıyla gidip hesaba katılmayan şeydir.

strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.1.3	water-fed tree; enduring leaf	The commentary sets rain held in rock hollows against vegetation that dries into residue; Psalm 1's tree by irrigation channels bears fruit and does not wither, making lasting nourishment the counterpart to passing debris.

strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.7	grass and flower wither	The commentary identifies غثاء as dried vegetation carried off by a flood; Isaiah's grass and flower wither, portraying created vitality as transient and preparing the contrast with what endures.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.8	God's word stands forever	The commentary pairs a reminder that benefits with the hereafter as more abiding; Isaiah says the grass fades but God's word stands forever, giving divine speech the permanence absent from the residue.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.32.2	teaching falls as rain	The commentary says a reminder may benefit and defines benefit as help toward good; Moses describes his teaching as rain and dew, making instruction itself life-giving water.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.55.11	rain-like word accomplishes its purpose	The commentary joins stored water to a reminder that may help people reach good; Isaiah compares God's effective word to rain, saying it does not return empty but accomplishes its purpose, an explicit scriptural bridge from water to beneficial speech.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.25.4	dross removed from silver	The commentary includes foam on molten metal among the residue that separates from useful substance; Proverbs says removing dross from silver leaves material for the silversmith's vessel, a refining counterpart to foam departing while value remains.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.57.20	restless sea casts up mire	The commentary's flood carries surface debris that disperses; Isaiah's restless sea casts up mire and mud and cannot rest, using the water's refuse as an image of the wicked, while the surah's foam is what the current leaves behind.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.12	waters measured by the Creator	The commentary links its measured wadis to created rock hollows that collect rain; Isaiah asks who measured the waters and marked off the heavens, placing water's bounded order under the Creator's measure.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.114.8	rock becomes pool and flint spring	The commentary describes God-created hollows in rock that collect rainwater; Psalm 114 says God turns rock into a pool and flint into a spring, adding the reversal in which rock itself becomes a source of provision.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Heb.6.7	rain yields a useful crop	The commentary defines benefit as what helps attain good and sets retained water against useless residue; Hebrews pictures ground drinking repeated rain and producing a useful crop, explicitly joining water with benefit.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Heb.6.8	thorns rejected and burned	The commentary's dried plant matter becomes flood refuse that goes away; Hebrews contrasts useful crop with land bearing thorns and thistles, rejected and ending in fire, giving the unproductive growth an ethical and judgmental outcome.

strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.12.2	everlasting life	The commentary calls the hereafter better and more abiding than worldly life; Daniel's resurrection scene distinguishes everlasting life from disgrace, giving a concrete scriptural account of the lasting afterlife.
strong	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 3:4	hope of immortality	The commentary calls the hereafter more abiding; Wisdom says the righteous may seem to die but their hope is full of immortality, explaining how apparent loss can conceal a lasting good.
strong	tevrat	motif	2 Maccabees 7:9	resurrection to lasting life	The commentary says the hereafter is better and more abiding; the martyr in 2 Maccabees expects the King of the world to raise the dead to renewed life, placing endurance in bodily resurrection rather than present survival.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.1.9	waters gathered into one place	The commentary's rock hollows and its explanation of abundant water as water gathered both stress collected water; Genesis makes gathering the waters an act of creation, showing such pools within a larger scriptural ordering of water.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.55.10	rain waters the earth	The commentary describes sky-water collected in hollows and links water's benefit to good; Isaiah's rain waters the earth and makes it bring forth seed and bread, supplying the agricultural effect behind its water-and-benefit comparison.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.6	all flesh is grass	The commentary's dried plant residue belongs to the cycle of pasture becoming waste; Isaiah begins its grass-and-flower comparison by declaring all flesh grass, extending that transience from vegetation to human life.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.46.5	waters roar and foam	The commentary distinguishes flood foam that disperses from water that remains; in the psalm's tumultuous scene the waters roar and foam as mountains shake, making foam part of threatening upheaval rather than a sign of useful water.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.139.13	darkness cannot hide	The commentary says God knows the public and the hidden; the psalm says even darkness is not dark to God, making concealment itself no barrier to divine knowledge.
medium	tevrat	motif	Ta'anit 7a	Torah compared to descending water	The commentary makes the benefit of a reminder depend on its helping people reach good and imagines water gathered in hollows; Ta'anit 7a compares Torah to water that descends from high places to low and says Torah endures in the humble, giving receptivity a rabbinic interpretation.
weak	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Avot de-Rabbi Natan A 6:2	water drops wear stone; Torah study	The commentary imagines rain held in a rock hollow and a beneficial reminder as retained water; Rabbi Akiva's story has drops wear a stone and prompt him to begin Torah study, turning the rock-water meeting into an image of instruction's effect rather than storage.

strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.4.14	water springing up to eternal life	The commentary connects water held in rock hollows with the hereafter's greater permanence; Jesus says the water he gives becomes a spring welling up to eternal life, joining water's benefit to enduring life.

strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.22.1	river of the water of life	The commentary links water gathered and retained with the lasting hereafter; Revelation's final-city vision has the river of the water of life flowing from God's throne, making life-giving water an eschatological provision.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.22.2	fruit and leaves for healing	The commentary defines benefit as help toward good and sets it beside the abiding hereafter; Revelation's tree by the river bears fruit and leaves for the healing of nations, giving the final water scene a concrete benefit.

strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.1.24	all human glory like grass	The commentary's dried pasture becomes residue that disperses; Peter quotes Isaiah's grass and flower image for all flesh and human glory, extending the fading-vegetation picture to human life.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.7	rain-soaked ground produces useful growth	The commentary links rainwater and benefit; Hebrews says land drinks rain and yields a useful crop, an unusually close image-to-value correspondence.
